newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm after quiet dealing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm after quiet dealing.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firmer against the dollar for the sixth session in a row on Monday after what dealers said was light selling of dollars in a market quiet ahead of U.S. inflation data Tuesday.
"I feel some went short (dollars), but the market will not show a fixed trend until some major event occurs," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.8 and 1.0 centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.9450/7.9500 and 7.9440/7.9460 per dollar.
"The market is not going to move far as long as no heavy positions are traded," the trader added.

U.S. consumer price data are due to be released shortly before Mexican foreign exchange markets open on Tuesday. Dealers said they would look carefully at reaction to the data in the U.S. bond market.
Same-day peso contracts had closed mid-morning 0.1 of a centavo firmer at 7.9480/7.9510 per dollar.

Dealers said the peso could moderately reverse its recent strength later in the week due to demand for dollars ahead of the close of the first half of the year, and to hedge against the July 2 Federal Open Market Committee meeting and Mexican mid-term elections on July 6.
"There will be some pressure because of the elections...the peso may trade at more than eight per dollar," a dealer said. (( -- Alexis Quiones, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9555))
